families.name: Live model, re-tuned (control)
families.idea: The model already live (bell-curve fair value vs the ask), re-tuned on a wider grid. It is the control: a new idea has to do better than simply re-tuning what we have.

families.name: Pyth open-print fair value
families.idea: Pyth-exact, no intra-window price. Fair value of YES at the start of the window from Pyth's own quarter-hour prints: this hour's recent rate of windows that ended exactly unchanged (an unchanged price settles YES) plus a tilt from the previous window's Pyth move. Buy in the first minutes when the ask is below that by the edge.

families.name: Pyth previous-window bet
families.idea: Pyth-exact. At the first minute, bet with (trend) or against (reversal) the previous window's Pyth move when it was at least pz quarter-hour standard deviations, if the ask is no more than max_price.

families.name: Unchanged-price YES
families.idea: Pyth-exact. YES wins when Pyth ends the window exactly at the opening print. In hours where that has happened often lately (trailing 14 days, same ET hour), buy YES early if it costs no more than 0.5 + half the tie rate - edge.

families.name: Favourite / long-shot (quotes only)
families.idea: Kalshi quotes only (they already reflect the live Pyth price). Late in the window, buy whichever side's ask sits in a price band: favourites (55-98c) if traders under-price near-certainties, long shots (2-45c) if they under-price comebacks. Settled by Pyth, so the outcome is exact.

families.name: Quote momentum (quotes only)
families.idea: Kalshi quotes only. When the YES mid has moved by at least d over the last L minutes, follow the move (traders are slow to price the live Pyth move) or fade it (they over-react).

families.name: Live model + Pyth unchanged-price chance
families.idea: The live bell-curve fair value on the Yahoo path (as lab4), plus the Pyth-exact chance that the window ends exactly unchanged (which settles YES): fair YES = tie + (1 - tie) x model.

families.name: Per-coin tuning with shrinkage
families.idea: One rule for all 9 coins, but each coin gets its own settings, chosen by that coin's own results plus the all-coin average (shrinkage), so thin data can't drive it alone.

families.name: Ensemble of the best survivors
families.idea: For each coin, combine the 2-3 families with the best walk-forward record into one first-to-fire rule (one bet per market).
